answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a costly, non-transferable reputation token earned only through verified work: a single identity grows like a vine, branching through completed tasks, while each fake copy must pay the full staking cost again. A shared reputation graph then scores agents by the pearl-like quality of their attestations, and a nebula of independent verifiers samples and audits random transactions, so creating thousands of cheap identities costs more than any reward they could extract.
